draft.title: The rise of new powers
card: After 1991 the United States had the largest economy and the strongest military. By the 2000s some other economies were growing much faster than its own.

From the late 1970s China opened its economy to trade and foreign investment. It became a major manufacturer and exporter, and by 2010 its economy was the second largest in the world, behind only the United States.
India, Brazil and other countries also grew quickly. Their rise gave more weight to groups such as the G20, which included these economies alongside older powers.
Economic growth gives a country more influence in trade, investment and diplomacy. By 2011 power was beginning to shift away from the United States, though it remained the strongest military power.
draft.remember: Fast economic growth in China and others began to shift global power by 2011, but the United States was still the leading military power.

a.q: Why did the rise of China matter for the world order by 2011?
opts: Its economic growth gave it more influence in world affairs
Its military had overtaken the United States and ended its lead
Its growth stopped trade between the United States and others
Its government joined the G20 in place of the United States
a.why: China's fast growth made it the second largest economy, which gave it more influence in trade and diplomacy. The claim that its military had overtaken the United States is wrong: the United States remained the strongest military power.
a.clue: Think about what economic growth gives a country.

b.q: A historian says that by 2011 global power was beginning to shift, but the United States had not been replaced. Which evidence best supports this view?
opts: China and India grew fast, while the US kept its military lead
China became the second largest economy, so the US lost influence
The G20 gave India and Brazil a voice, so the US left world affairs
India and Brazil grew fast, so the US economy became the smallest
b.why: The first option shows both parts of the claim: new economies were rising, yet the United States kept its military lead. The second goes too far, because the United States was still the largest economy and kept great influence, so power had only begun to shift.
b.clue: The claim has two parts, and the evidence must cover both.
